purpose: Publication reliability measured separately from model coordination quality.
write_contract: Each operation writes its own uniquely named field and payload hash. Same-artifact operations additionally write one shared field with distinct submitted values. Every independently published field must survive. The final shared-field value must be one submitted value, and at least two independent replica readbacks must agree after writer completion to establish convergence. This protocol does not impose expected-head CAS, semantic conflict rejection, or preservation of both shared-field values. A committing local evaluation must be observed exactly once; final inventory alone cannot detect replay of identical writes.
concurrency: Release both writers at a barrier in each registered round. Start intervals must overlap in every round. Burst round offsets are scheduled from the first barrier, not from completion of the previous write.
observation: An external adapter produces one receipt per operation, independent readback of that operation's field, and a final complete inventory from a fresh observer after all writers exit. Bind the observations to the plan SHA-256 and identify the fixture/build and transport. No model session is needed.
failure_policy: Retain every registered operation and failed case. Publication retries inside the product are counted; the adapter must not replay an uncertain write. Recovery must identify readback or retained-publication resolution. Missing evidence is unknown, never a zero latency or a quality score.
quality: No reliability metric contributes points to the frozen coordination quality rubric. Past scenarios, protocols and runs remain unchanged.
scope: Synthetic scorer tests prove measurement machinery only. Actual reliability evidence requires external receipts from the real product fixture or deployed service; label the exercised boundary explicitly.
